title: City Birds Fly Away Sooner From Women Than Men
summary:
Here is a puzzle for bird watchers: city birds seem to fly away sooner when a woman walks toward them than when a man does, and scientists do not know why.

An international team of researchers tested this in parks and green spaces in five European countries: Czechia, France, Germany, Poland and Spain. Men and women of similar height, wearing similar clothes, walked straight toward birds. The scientists measured how close each person could get before the bird took off. This is called the flight initiation distance.

On average, men could get about one meter closer than women. The same pattern showed up in every country and in all 37 bird species studied, including great tits, house sparrows, blackbirds, jumpy magpies and usually relaxed pigeons. The study, based on 2,701 observations, was published in the journal People and Nature.

"I fully believe our results," said Professor Daniel Blumstein of the University of California, Los Angeles, "but I can't explain them right now."

Scientists have a few guesses. Birds might notice smells, differences in body shape, or the way people walk. But these ideas have not been tested yet. Dr. Federico Morelli of the University of Turin called the mystery "maybe the most interesting part of our study."

Dr. Yanina Benedetti of the Czech University of Life Sciences Prague said she was surprised, as a woman working in the field. Many animal studies assume a human observer has no effect, she said, but that was not true for these birds.

The researchers say their findings are still early, and more studies are needed. For now, it seems the birds sharing our cities notice details about people that we hardly notice ourselves.
why_it_matters: The study shows that wild animals in cities may read subtle human cues, and that scientists cannot assume a human observer has no effect on the animals they study.

background_read: Wild animals constantly decide whether people nearby are a danger, and fleeing too early or too late can cost them food or safety.
Scientists often measure this by walking toward an animal and noting how close they get before it flies or runs away.
City birds see many people every day, so they may learn to read small clues about humans that country birds never need to notice.
Researchers use careful methods, such as matching walkers' height and clothing, so that only one difference is being tested at a time.
Article_Structure: LEAD: City birds fly away sooner when approached by women than by men, and scientists cannot explain why
METHOD: Men and women matched for height and clothing walked toward birds in parks
├─ WHERE: Czechia, France, Germany, Poland and Spain
RESULT: Men got about one meter closer, across all 37 species and every country
EXPERTS: Daniel Blumstein, Federico Morelli and Yanina Benedetti react to the puzzle
POSSIBLE CAUSES: Smells, body shape or walking style, all still untested
OPEN QUESTION: What exactly are the birds detecting?
